forces.title: Weak consumer confidence and disposable income pressure
forces.description: Consumer confidence is low, and disposable incomes are under pressure, causing consumers to delay discretionary purchases like white-goods or opt for cheaper alternatives. This weakness in demand is exacerbated by a subdued housing market, limiting natural demand flow into the household equipment sector, forcing businesses to focus on price-sensitive demand.

forces.title: Demand for energy-efficient and smart appliances
forces.description: Despite overall weak consumer confidence, there is steady interest in energy-efficient and smart appliances. This trend, along with replacement purchases, provides a source of resilience for the household equipment sector, offering defensive categories for businesses to focus on amidst price-sensitive demand and margin pressure, and potentially capturing growth opportunities in a challenging market.

forces.title: Rising input costs and freight disruption for Textiles
forces.description: The Middle East crisis and oil price volatility have caused a 10-20% increase in textile input prices (gas, petrochemicals). Rerouting has added 10-14 days to transit times and pushed some freight costs up by 300%. These rising costs, coupled with promotion-led demand, squeeze margins and increase working-capital requirements for textiles and apparel manufacturers, making the sector highly vulnerable.

forces.title: Nearshoring and supply-chain diversification in Textiles
forces.description: Businesses in the textiles and apparel sector are accelerating moves towards nearshoring, diversifying suppliers, and increasing inventory buffers to build greater supply-chain resilience. This structural shift moves away from just-in-time models, but it also increases working-capital requirements, especially for mid-market retailers facing promotional demand and cost inflation, impacting operational strategies and financial planning.

forces.title: Intensifying competition from ultra-low-cost online players
forces.description: UK retailers face increasing margin pressure from ultra-low-cost overseas online platforms, particularly from China. These players are resetting expectations on price, choice, and convenience, significantly impacting price-sensitive categories and lower-margin segments within consumer durables and apparel. This trend has seen nearly half of UK shoppers purchase from such platforms, forcing domestic manufacturers to adapt their pricing and value propositions.

forces.title: Health-conscious consumption driving fashion demand
forces.description: A broader shift towards more health-conscious consumption, potentially accelerated by weight-loss drugs (GLP-1s), is expected to benefit the clothing category. Changing body profiles may lead to more frequent wardrobe refresh cycles, creating opportunities for manufacturers in the textiles and apparel sector, despite adding complexity to sizing and inventory management, suggesting a need for increased flexibility in production.

forces.title: Poor generative AI search visibility for luxury brands
forces.description: Luxury brands face a significant risk from poor generative engine optimization (GEO). With 70% of luxury-related queries not mentioning a specific brand, third-party content dominates AI search citations. Brands with weak GEO risk being bypassed by AI agents, leading to lost customer discovery and reduced narrative control in critical purchasing stages, impacting brand perception and sales in the luxury goods market.
forces.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

forces.title: AI-augmented sales assistance for luxury customer interactions
forces.description: AI-augmented sales assistance is the most advanced customer-facing innovation in luxury, with every multi-brand group developing or piloting solutions. This technology, along with AI digital personalization, has the potential to transform client interactions by improving sales processes and elevating customer experiences, though widespread adoption is still developing at the Maison level, presenting a significant opportunity for competitive differentiation.
forces.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

forces.title: Rising adoption of AI and resale channels in luxury
forces.description: The luxury sector is seeing a rising use of AI and resale channels for shopping. More US customers use AI for inspiration, while Chinese entry-level clients engage with AI across the shopping journey. Secondhand channels are increasingly important for higher-spending US clients, driven by the "thrill of the hunt" and bargains, reshaping the customer journey for luxury goods and requiring brands to manage these new touchpoints actively.
forces.source_title: The State of Luxury: What US and Chinese clients reveal about the sector’s future

forces.title: Emotional connection driving luxury brand desirability
forces.description: Emotional connection is the top driver of luxury brand desirability in the US and China, surpassing traditional factors like craft and heritage. Consumers are increasingly drawn to brands that feel personally meaningful and reflect their identity. This trend particularly benefits categories such as jewellery, which is strongly associated with identity, emotion, and self-expression, compelling brands to focus on storytelling and cultural relevance.
forces.source_title: The State of Luxury: What US and Chinese clients reveal about the sector’s future

forces.title: Agentic commerce reshaping demand and retail competition
forces.description: Agentic commerce, where AI influences discovery and executes transactions on consumers' behalf, is a seismic shift for retail. It changes how competition works, with retailers competing to be selected by algorithms. This impacts consumer durables and apparel manufacturers by prioritizing platforms and brands that are legible, trusted, and performant, risking bypass for others, thus demanding adaptation in product data and fulfillment reliability.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new e‑commerce agenda: How AI is resetting growth and competition

forces.title: AI transformation for softline retail (apparel, footwear, luxury beauty)
forces.description: Softline retailers, including those in apparel, footwear, and luxury beauty, are expected to see the largest upside from end-to-end AI transformation. This is due to their generous EBITDA margins, complex assortments, less predictable demand, and strong consumer need for personalization, offering substantial gains through optimization of pricing, promotions, and assortment, driving significant economic value for the sector.
forces.source_title: Rewiring retail in Europe: The AI imperative

forces.title: Intense competition and changing consumer behavior for Textiles
forces.description: The textiles sector faces strong competition from US and Chinese online marketplaces, coupled with changing consumer behavior like reduced brand loyalty and increased interest in second-hand markets. This exacerbates soft demand and margin pressure from industrial energy costs and wage inflation, leading to low order visibility and elevated working-capital and insolvency risks, particularly for smaller firms in the UK.

forces.title: Cautious consumer spending on household equipment upgrades
forces.description: Consumers remain cautious, leading to weak spending intentions for household equipment, especially for AI-driven upgrades of new products. There's only a moderate appetite for early-stage technology, and strong competition from Asian firms further weighs on the sector. This soft demand, coupled with high household bills, creates challenging trading conditions and persistent pressure, evidenced by recent business failures in the UK market.

forces.title: AI-driven product upgrades in household equipment
forces.description: The household equipment sector is undergoing a structural shift towards AI-driven product upgrades and smart home automation. While current consumer appetite for early-stage technology remains moderate, this trend, alongside demand for sustainability/eco-friendly products, is an ongoing driver of growth, offering differentiation opportunities in a saturated market and requiring strategic investment in innovation and product development.

forces.title: AI reshaping customer journey and competitive advantage
forces.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping the customer journey and becoming a core driver of competitive advantage across consumer industries, including durables and apparel. AI-driven efficiencies and redefined product discovery are creating an enduring paradigm for consumer engagement. Manufacturers must integrate AI into their strategies to maintain relevance and drive growth in this evolving market, with a focus on human-led intelligence for sustained success.
forces.source_title: Retail and Consumer Trends 2026: Human-led intelligence

viewpoints.title: UK Household Equipment sector constrained by weak consumer confidence and income pressure
viewpoints.description: The UK household equipment sector faces weakness due to low consumer confidence and pressure on disposable incomes, leading to delayed white-goods purchases and trading down. Subdued housing activity further limits demand. However, replacement purchases and interest in energy-efficient and smart appliances offer some resilience. Businesses should adapt to price-sensitive demand and focus on defensive categories that leverage these trends to mitigate ongoing margin pressure.

viewpoints.title: UK Textiles and Apparel sector under pressure from weak economic conditions
viewpoints.description: The UK textiles and apparel sector faces heightened pressure from weak economic conditions and disruption due to the Middle East crisis. Input prices, especially for oil, gas, and petrochemicals, have risen by 10-20%, while freight costs are up by as much as 300% due to rerouting. Demand remains stable but fragile, heavily reliant on promotions, leading to increased working-capital requirements and greater exposure for mid-market retailers.

viewpoints.title: Luxury companies risk losing customers without strong AI search visibility
viewpoints.description: Luxury companies risk losing potential customers and narrative control if they don't address generative engine optimization (GEO). AI-generated search answers are reshaping brand discoverability, with 75% of luxury prompts expressing discovery or comparison intent. Currently, only 10% of Maisons consider themselves strong on generative visibility, highlighting a critical need for GEO strategies to build relevant brand awareness, reinvent acquisition, and enrich the sales process.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

viewpoints.title: Pandora aims for thoughtful, crafted online jewelry interactions at scale
viewpoints.description: Pandora's Senior Vice President of E-commerce, Jesper Damsgaard, states that the company's goal is to make every online interaction for its jewelry feel thoughtful and crafted, acknowledging the difficulty of achieving this at scale. This highlights the luxury sector's challenge and opportunity in leveraging digital channels to maintain brand essence and elevate customer experiences, aligning with the broader trend of AI reshaping discovery and customer interaction.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new e‑commerce agenda: How AI is resetting growth and competition

viewpoints.title: IKEA aims for immersive customer relationships using AI in home furnishings
viewpoints.description: Parag Parekh, Chief Digital Officer of Ingka Group (IKEA), states that AI is fundamentally changing customer interactions from transactional to immersive, solution-oriented relationships in home furnishings. This includes AI for customer experience, supply chain optimization, and back-office productivity, with strong returns seen in goal-based order allocation and cross-sell/upsell personalization. He emphasizes prioritization of AI initiatives to avoid spreading efforts too thinly.
viewpoints.source_title: Rewiring retail in Europe: The AI imperative

viewpoints.title: ADEO leverages AI for product information and visual inspiration in home improvement
viewpoints.description: Matthieu Grymonprez, CDIO of ADEO, highlights how AI is transforming home improvement by optimizing supply chain, sourcing, and in-store productivity. Generative AI is crucial for managing product information at scale, automating product descriptions, and enabling features like "Shop the Look" for visual inspiration, significantly expanding online assortment and enhancing customer experience. He notes the importance of a solid digital foundation for AI to be effective.
viewpoints.source_title: Rewiring retail in Europe: The AI imperative

viewpoints.title: UK Textiles sector faces tough trading amid weak demand and digital competition
viewpoints.description: The UK textiles and apparel sector is in a tough trading environment due to soft demand, increased digital footprint on retail sales, and strong competition from US and Chinese online marketplaces. Changing consumer behavior, including lower brand loyalty and appetite for second-hand markets, contribute to low cashflow visibility and persistent cost pressure. Working-capital and insolvency risks remain elevated in weaker parts of the market.

viewpoints.title: UK Household Equipment constrained by cautious consumers and AI upgrade appetite
viewpoints.description: The household equipment sector remains constrained by cautious consumers and weak spending intentions towards AI-driven upgrades for new-generation products. A moderate appetite for early-stage technology upgrades and competitiveness challenges with Asian firms weigh on the outlook. Trading conditions mirror broader retail softness, and recent business failures underscore persistent pressure in the sector, despite opportunities in home automation and eco-friendly products.

demand_drivers.description: Consumers are attracted to ultra-low prices, driving purchases from these platforms.

market_sizing.methodology: Annual spending by UK shoppers on Chinese ultra-low-price online platforms. This represents 5% of total non-food online sales in the UK, impacting various consumer goods, including those manufactured in the Consumer Durables & Apparel sector.

demand_drivers.description: 75% of luxury prompts express discovery or comparison intent, driven by generative AI search tools.

new_opportunities.description: Optimizing online presence to rank well in AI-generated search results, including claiming a territory, aligning content to shopping intent, prioritizing off-site content, curating consumer reviews, and maintaining fresh, readable content.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of consumer search behavior on generative engines for luxury goods, focusing on how brands are surfaced and cited. Insights derived from 9,049 luxury-intent prompts across 8 markets (US, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, UK, Japan, South Korea) from July 2025 to January 2026.
market_sizing.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

demand_drivers.description: Clients are increasingly drawn to brands that feel personally meaningful, reflecting their identity and values.

pnl_drivers.description: Previous price increases by leading fashion brands without corresponding product innovation turned off aspirational clients, dampening appetite for fashion.

market_sizing.methodology: Global luxury market growth rate, based on McKinsey Luxury Model, McKinsey Global Fashion Index, McKinsey Beauty Model, Euromonitor, analyst reports, company results, and expert interviews. This applies to personal luxury goods including fashion, leather goods, watches, and jewelry.
market_sizing.source_title: The State of Luxury: What US and Chinese clients reveal about the sector’s future

demand_drivers.description: Brands need to re-engage established and aspirational clients who have been turned off by price hikes and a weaker entry-level offering.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated value of the "critical middle" client segment in the global luxury personal goods market (established and aspirational clients). These clients have been underserved by luxury brands focusing on ultra-wealthy clients, representing a significant potential growth pool.
market_sizing.source_title: The State of Luxury: What US and Chinese clients reveal about the sector’s future

demand_drivers.description: Beauty attracts the strongest intent to increase spending across markets and client tiers, particularly in China, driven by its lower price point and repeat purchase cycle.

new_opportunities.description: Higher intent to spend on footwear than bags among aspirational US clients and across all tiers in China. This indicates potential for shoes to become a key accessible item for clients to engage with luxury brands.

market_sizing.methodology: Survey of over 2,000 luxury clients across spending tiers in the US and China, analyzing expected changes to future spend in the next 2-3 years by category and client tier.
market_sizing.source_title: The State of Luxury: What US and Chinese clients reveal about the sector’s future

pnl_drivers.description: AI can improve EBITDA by 6-8 percentage points for hardline retailers through a balanced mix of commercial and operational value levers, increasing efficiency and optimizing processes.

market_sizing.methodology: AI-driven EBITDA improvement for European hardline retailers (non-apparel, durable goods like electronics and appliances) is projected at 6-8 percentage points, translating to an economic value of €50-60 billion for Europe's retail sector.
market_sizing.source_title: Rewiring retail in Europe: The AI imperative
